findings.citation_text: Recent work, such as MoiréVib and MoiréPose [30, 31], has showcased the power of moiré amplification for motion sensing.
findings.reasoning: Cited as a representative example of moiré amplification for motion sensing. Grouped with [30], so attribution uncertainty.

findings.citation_text: The spatial frequency of the resulting moiré pattern is given by f_m = |f1 - f2| [1, 30, 31].
findings.reasoning: Directly cites MoiréVib for the core formula governing moiré pattern spatial frequency, which is foundational to the theoretical model.

findings.citation_text: Formally, gratings 1 and 2 have nearly identical spatial frequencies, denoted as f1 and f2, respectively. The spatial frequency of the resulting moiré pattern is given by f_m = |f1 - f2|[1, 30, 31].
findings.reasoning: Citing MoiréVib alongside other references for the fundamental moiré theory used to derive amplification.

findings.citation_text: The combined optical intensity at position p_m is modeled as the product of their individual intensities [1, 30, 31]: I(p_m,t) = I1(p_m,t) I2(p_m).
findings.reasoning: MoiréVib is cited as support for the multiplicative intensity model in the general moiré pattern derivation.

findings.citation_text: Its components along the X- and Y-axes can be represented as a spatial frequency vector f1 [1, 30, 31]: f1 = [f_x1, f_y1]^T = f1 [|cos θ1|, |sin θ1|]^T.
findings.reasoning: Cites MoiréVib for the spatial frequency vector formulation, essential for modeling arbitrary orientations.

findings.citation_text: prior work has proposed using two cameras to increase the frame rate from 30∼60 fps up to around 300 fps [31].
findings.reasoning: Mentions MoiréVib's dual-camera approach as a baseline that achieves only 300 fps, highlighting its insufficiency for audio. Sets up the challenge that MoiréEar addresses.

findings.citation_text: Prior work has relied on analyzing video frames [30–32, 45]; however, such methods are limited by low sample rates, which are insufficient for reconstructing audio signals at kilohertz frequencies.
findings.reasoning: MoiréVib is grouped with other prior works as relying on video frames; used as background to motivate the photodiode approach.

findings.citation_text: For a typical camera, the measurement frame rate is limited to tens of frames per second [27, 31].
findings.reasoning: Cites MoiréVib as an example of camera-based moiré sensing with limited frame rate, reinforcing the limitation.

findings.citation_text: More recently, Ning et al. [31] presented MoiréVib, enabling high-accuracy vibration sensing in dynamic environments.
findings.reasoning: Described as a representative recent work in moiré-based sensing. Stance is neutral as it's a factual description.

findings.citation_text: Although these works highlight the strong potential of moiré-based sensing, their performance remains constrained by controlled setups, dedicated gratings, and limited sample rates. Consequently, existing moiré-based sensing approaches are not yet suitable for capturing full-bandwidth speech information.
findings.reasoning: Points out limitations of prior moiré-based sensing, including MoiréVib (via grouped reference), contrasting with MoiréEar's capabilities.
